concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 1 - Execute Student-Only Gating Training Loop
concerns.text: User Story 1 has no associated Success Criteria. All other user stories reference at least one SC (e.g., SC-001, SC-002, SC-003, SC-004), but there is no SC‑### that ties to US‑1, leaving the story under‑specified.
FR-001 cross‑reference uses '(See US-1)' but the user stories are labeled 'User Story 1' (no US‑1 identifier). The reference cannot be resolved.
FR-002 cross‑reference uses '(See US-2)' while the corresponding story is 'User Story 2'. Identifier mismatch prevents proper traceability.
FR-003 cross‑reference uses '(See US-3)' but the story is named 'User Story 3'.
FR-006 cross‑reference uses '(See US-1)' which does not exist; should refer to 'User Story 1'.
SC-001 mentions a 'GRPO' baseline that is never defined elsewhere in the specification, creating an undefined term and breaking internal consistency of success criteria.

Success Criterion SC-001 references a GRPO baseline (Success_GRPO) but the specification contains no functional requirement that generates or records this baseline data. Without an FR to produce the GRPO success metric, the required comparison (Success_Student - Success_GRPO) ≥ 0.8 × (Success_Baseline - Success_GRPO) cannot be instantiated, making the criterion untestable.

The specification omits any requirement to compute and report the Pearson correlation coefficient between the student‑only heuristic scores (token entropy $H_t$ and context stability $S_t$) and the original teacher‑student confidence‑gap scores. The idea explicitly states this analysis is needed to validate whether the teacher signal adds value, and Constitution Principle VII mandates it. Add a functional requirement (e.g., FR‑007) and corresponding success criterion to capture this correlation analysis.

The research question and SC‑001 claim a causal relationship ('Student‑Only gating can replace the teacher‑student confidence gap') but the experimental design is purely comparative/observational and does not control for confounding factors, making the causal inference unsupported.

The plan does not specify a sufficient number of independent runs; earlier drafts indicated only 5 runs per variant (total 30 runs). This sample size yields low statistical power for detecting the claimed ≥60 % CPU‑time reduction and ≥80 % performance‑retention, even with bootstrapping.

Early‑stopping when the average reward reaches 0.8 causes the Student‑Only variant to terminate earlier than the Baseline, conflating per‑step CPU‑time reduction (SC‑002) with faster convergence. Comparing per‑step cost under differing episode counts introduces bias.

The fallback to a Kaggle T4 GPU if the model cannot load on CPU introduces a hardware confound: runs that switch to GPU will have different CPU‑time characteristics, violating the assumption that per‑step CPU cost is comparable across variants.
